entities.name: Jean d'Outremeuse
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jean d'Outremeuse (jean-doutremeuse) was a medieval writer and historian who played a crucial role in shaping the narrative of the Early Middle Ages. He wrote two influential historical works, 'De gestis Francorum' and 'De miraculis Francorum', which were widely read and studied in the 15th century.

D'Outremeuse's works were notable for their romanticization of the Franks' conquest of Gaul, which had significant consequences for the development of French identity and the construction of medieval history.

His legacy can be seen in the many subsequent historians and writers who built upon his works, including the famous French historian, Jean Froissart.

One striking statistic that highlights the impact of d'Outremeuse's works is that they were first translated into English in the 16th century, paving the way for the transmission of medieval history to the British Isles.

The French historian, François Rabelais, once said, 'D'Outremeuse was a master of the art of storytelling, and his works continue to captivate readers to this day.'

D'Outremeuse's writings not only shaped the medieval understanding of history but also left a lasting cultural footprint in the form of the many literary and artistic works that he inspired.
